title: SyncSpace
overview: SyncSpace is a browser extension that keeps bookmarks, tab groups, and extension profiles in sync across every device a user works from. We built it as an offline-first system so browsing organization never breaks, even on a flaky connection.
challenge: {"title":"Bookmarks that fall out of sync the moment you switch devices","description":"Power users routinely work across three or more machines, but browser-native bookmark sync is unreliable, slow, and prone to silently overwriting changes when multiple devices edit the same folder offline.","painPoints":["Bookmark and tab-group state drifted between devices with no conflict resolution","No offline support — sync simply failed without a live connection","Direct, unbatched writes to the sync backend caused excessive network overhead","Deep browser API integration required careful permission and security handling"],"businessImpact":["Users lost trust in the extension after experiencing overwritten bookmark folders","High network chatter increased backend costs and battery drain on laptops"]}
goals: ["Guarantee bookmark and tab-group consistency across unlimited devices","Make sync resilient to offline and intermittent connections","Reduce network overhead from constant small sync writes","Keep the extension lightweight with no visible sync delay"]
solution: {"title":"An offline-first sync engine with real conflict resolution","description":"We rebuilt sync around a local-first queue: every change is written locally first, then reconciled against the server using a hierarchical tree-merge algorithm designed specifically for nested bookmark structures.","highlights":["Offline-first sync queue with local storage caching and exponential backoff","Hierarchical tree-reconciliation algorithm for multi-device bookmark merges","Rate-limited, batched Supabase transactions to cut network overhead","Deep integration with chrome.bookmarks, chrome.tabGroups, and chrome.management APIs"]}
workflow: [{"title":"Browser API audit","description":"Mapped every bookmark, tab-group, and extension-management API needed, along with the permission model required to use them safely."},{"title":"Offline queue design","description":"Built the local-first write queue and retry-with-backoff logic before touching the sync backend, so the extension worked fully offline from the start."},{"title":"Merge algorithm","description":"Designed and tested a tree-reconciliation algorithm against real-world conflict scenarios — simultaneous edits, deletions, and folder moves across devices."},{"title":"Backend + batching","description":"Connected the queue to Supabase with transaction batching and rate limiting to minimize round trips."},{"title":"Cross-browser QA","description":"Validated behavior across Chrome, Edge, and Brave, then shipped to the Web Store with staged rollout."}]
architecture: ["Local-first write queue backed by browser storage","Hierarchical tree-reconciliation engine for structural merges","Supabase Postgres with row-level security per user","Batched, rate-limited sync transactions","Exponential backoff retry layer for unreliable connections"]
features: ["Real-time bookmark and tab-group sync across devices","Full offline support with automatic catch-up sync","Conflict-free folder merges, even with simultaneous edits","Extension profile sync alongside bookmarks and tabs"]
uiHighlights: ["Native-feeling popup UI built with ShadCN components","Visual sync-status indicator with per-device activity log","Zero-config onboarding — sync starts on install"]
challengesFaced: ["Resolving simultaneous edits to the same bookmark folder from two offline devices","Working within strict browser extension security and permission constraints","Avoiding excessive Supabase writes from frequent small bookmark changes","Keeping merge logic correct across deeply nested folder structures"]
solutionsImplemented: ["Built a tree-diff merge algorithm that resolves structural conflicts deterministically","Scoped extension permissions to the minimum required APIs, reviewed against store policy","Introduced write batching and debouncing, cutting network overhead by over 40%","Added recursive test fixtures covering multi-level folder merge scenarios"]
results: ["Reduced sync-related network overhead by more than 40%","Eliminated reported cases of bookmark data loss after launch","Sync now completes in under 2 seconds on reconnect after extended offline use","Maintained a 4.8-star average rating on the Chrome Web Store"]
testimonial: {"name":"Marcus Webb","role":"Founder","company":"SyncSpace","quote":"The offline-first sync engine Brain Stack built solved a problem we'd struggled with for months. Bookmarks just stay in sync now — no drama, no overwritten folders.","image":"/images/testimonials/customer-2.webp"}
lessonsLearned: ["Local-first architecture should be the default for any tool that touches personal device state","Tree-reconciliation is worth the upfront complexity when structural data can conflict","Batching writes early prevents backend cost surprises as usage scales"]
